# Sizes, in BYTES, of the self-host driver binaries CI already builds, plus
# the compiler's own output for itself — checked against every run by
# scripts/ci-check-driver-sizes (#6826).
#
# WHICH BINARY IS "THE SELF-HOST BINARY": fern.fern/stage2, named below as the
# tracked artifact. It is compiler/fern.fern, the whole self-hosted
# compiler CLI, COMPILED BY ITSELF (the fern.fern driver, built by the pin,
# compiling its own source — the bootstrap chain's stage2), so it is the one
# row that moves with the current compiler's code generation, and it is the
# number to quote when talking about self-host binary size (#4109's "well
# under half" target is against it). Every other row is a driver built by the
# PINNED stage0 compiler (bootstrap/stage0.lock): those rows move with the
# drivers' sources and the stdlib, never with a codegen change in the current
# compiler, and a pin refresh moves them all. `fern.fern` is the pin's build
# of the CLI (stage1); `asm_ir_run` is the front-end plus the x86-64 IR
# backend, `wasm_ir_run` the front-end plus the wasm one, and so on. They are
# recorded because they are free to record and they localise a regression to
# a backend — NOT because they are interchangeable. Quoting one against
# another is how #4109 acquired a bogus "the epic is 4x off": a 245 MB CLI
# figure compared with a 59 MB wasm_ir_run figure.
#
# tracked-artifact: fern.fern/stage2
#
# HOW THIS IS MEASURED. The `driver-sizes` job of test-e2e-selfhost.yml reads
# the driver names out of this file, builds every one of them
# (TestSelfHostWarmStockDriver; fern.fern/stage2 is the warmed fern.fern run
# over its own source), stats each into FERN_DRIVER_SIZE_REPORT, and compares
# that report against this file. Both compilers' output is deterministic per
# input, so a given commit yields the same byte count on any runner — a
# difference here is a real change in the sources, the stdlib, the pin or
# (for fern.fern/stage2) the current compiler's codegen, not runner noise. A
# pin refresh re-baselines every pin-built row, in the same PR.
#
# ENFORCED, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Drift past FERN_SIZE_TOLERANCE_PERCENT (5% by
# default) is a job-summary line, a warning annotation and a FAILED
# `driver-sizes` job. A SHRINK is flagged too: an un-updated baseline after a
# win silently raises the ceiling the next regression is measured against,
# which is how 16% of growth went unnoticed for eight days — and, in the other
# direction, how a 3.0 MB win was never recorded either (#7519).
#
# A DRIVER THAT WENT UNMEASURED FAILS TOO. `driver-sizes` sets
# FERN_SIZE_REPORT_COMPLETE=1, so a name in this file that reached no report is
# a finding instead of a row nobody notices is absent. The job used to union
# four per-job slices, each of which checked only the drivers it linked, so a
# five-row table ending in "every driver is within 5% of its baseline" was
# indistinguishable from a fifteen-row one — which is how the drivers grew 2.3x
# with the gate green.
#
# WHEN A NUMBER MOVES ON PURPOSE, update it in the same PR — the job summary
# prints the corrected lines ready to paste. Keep the reason in the PR, not
# here; this file is a set of current facts.
#
# x86-64. The `driver-sizes` job is x86-only (the aarch64 lane skips the x86
# driver builds), so there is one architecture to baseline and no per-arch split.
#
# REFRESHED after #6928 (.bss laid out last, so the ELF writer's zero-fill
# trim reaches it). TWO INDEPENDENT MOVEMENTS ARE FOLDED INTO THESE NUMBERS
# and they point opposite ways — do not read either figure as one effect:
#
#   1. The five drivers that link the strbuf runtime fell 78-84%, because
#      `__fern_strbuf_data`'s 64 MiB .bss reservation is no longer written to
#      the file. Measured on one host, same tree, fix in vs out: fern.fern
#      85,581,884 -> 18,473,012. That is the #6928 win and it is confined to
#      those five; for a driver without strbuf the output is BYTE-IDENTICAL
#      with and without the fix (verified on irlower_run).
#   2. Every driver also grew ~348 KB of .text against the previous baseline,
#      from self-host source changes that landed between the two refreshes.
#      That is why the ten non-strbuf drivers show +3.0% to +8.9% here: it is
#      main moving, not a codegen regression.
#
# Refreshed before that after #4111 (8-byte operand-stack slots + real
# push/pop on the x86-64 backend), which cut code density ~19% across the
# board.
#
# Refreshed before that after #6894 (exit-sweep drop outlining), which cut
# every driver: the tracked artifact by 42.5%, the front-end-only drivers by
# over 80%.
#
# THE PREVIOUS REFRESH'S FIGURES DID NOT REPRODUCE, and the first complete
# comparison is what caught it. #7677 recorded fifteen numbers that read 13-16%
# HIGH against what the same tree links: thirteen of them tripped the shrink
# check on the first `driver-sizes` run, uniformly, on a diff that touches no
# compiler code. Three things were established before these numbers replaced
# them, because a baseline nobody can reproduce is how this file failed before:
#
#   1. The method reproduces CI EXACTLY. checker_modload_run rebuilt off-CI at
#      the head CI measured gives 7,053,860 against CI's 7,053,860 — the
#      determinism this file asserts, demonstrated rather than trusted.
#   2. It also DISCRIMINATES, which an agreeing number alone does not show.
#      Walking that driver back over the commits that touch its import closure
#      moves it 7,033,212 -> 7,205,244, so the measurement follows the source.
#   3. The old figure is not a stale checkout. checker_modload_run's closure is
#      unchanged between #7677's own commit and this one, so its size cannot
#      have moved in that window, and 8,171,948 — what #7677 wrote for it —
#      occurs nowhere in the surrounding history.
#
# So the drivers did not shrink; the previous numbers were wrong when written.
# What produced them is NOT known, and that is the honest state: they are not
# this tree's output at that commit, at the commit before it, or at any commit
# sampled around it. #7519's attribution of the GROWTH before #7677 stands on
# its own evidence and is unaffected.
#
# Every figure below is CI's own, from the `driver-sizes` job's union of the
# `cli` and three `warm` reports on the head that recorded them — the first
# time all fifteen were compared in one place. The two the union did not print
# (ssa_run, ssa_emit_run, both inside tolerance and so not in its paste block)
# were linked off-CI with the method item 1 validates.
#
# Note the two tiers: the three drivers at 3.1-3.7 MB link a front-end slice
# only, while the rest sit at 12-19 MB. A small driver moving 5% is a different
# quantity of bytes from the tracked artifact moving 5%; the percentage is what
# is compared, deliberately, so a small driver's regression is not lost inside a
# big one's noise.
#
# WHAT THE FIFTEEN DO NOT SEE (#7519). These drivers are not a sample of the
# compiler. Each links one import closure, and a module outside it contributes
# nothing to that driver's bytes — so a change of any size registers at its full
# cost against some of these numbers and as exactly zero against others. Three
# consequences, before you quote a figure or add a driver:
#
#   * SEVENTEEN MODULES ARE VISIBLE ONLY THROUGH fern.fern: both native back
#     ends (x86_native, arm64_native), elf, watbin, ssa_wasm, interp, printer,
#     constfold, literate, ferndoc, mvs, caps, platforms, visibility,
#     wit_decode, wit_compose, wit_proxy_world. A change
#     confined to one of them moves a single number in this file, and moves it
#     against the largest denominator here, where 300 KB is 0.8% and vanishes
#     under the tolerance. The claim above that the smaller drivers "localise a
#     regression to a backend" holds for the IR, asm and wasm-IR backends and
#     NOT for the native emitters, which have no localising driver at all.
#   * ONE LIBRARY MODULE IS LINKED BY NO BASELINED DRIVER:
#     wasm_objfile — reachable only from wasm_modload_run, which
#     wasm-wholecompiler-link builds as a WASM module rather than an x86-64
#     ELF, a size that does not belong in this file's one architecture.
#     Covering it means paying for an x86-64 link of a driver nothing else
#     needs. Three neighbours look like they belong on this list and do not:
#     builtins.fern is never imported — modloader READS it at runtime
#     (`read_file(dir + "builtins.fern")`), so it is a source input rather
#     than linked code — while pipeline.fern and wasm_units_probe.fern carry
#     their own `main` and are unbaselined PROGRAMS, not unlinked modules.
#   * FIVE DRIVERS COVER TWO CLOSURES: asm_pathprobe_run and asm_ir_elig_run
#     have identical import closures, as do wasm_ir_run, wasm_run and
#     wasm_runio_run. They differ in what their `main` reaches, not in what
#     they link, so the three wasm rows are close to one measurement.
#
# PICK THE DENOMINATOR THAT SEES YOUR CHANGE. A change confined to one module is
# honestly measured against the SMALLEST driver linking it, not against the
# tracked artifact: checker.fern -> checker_modload_run (3.7 MB), the front end
# or ssa -> ssa_run (3.1 MB), irlower.fern -> asm_ir_elig_run (12.0 MB).
# Dividing by the wrong one is not a small error. #7519 found the 311-loop
# checker migration registering EXACTLY 0 bytes against irlower_run, which does
# not link checker.fern at all, and found one irlower slice reading +6.8% or
# +9.2% for the same absolute growth depending only on which driver divided it.

# WHY checker_modload_run MOVED +5.5% (7053860 -> 7438860). Crediting a
# match-arm binding as an owned projection source in rhsTainted's FieldAccess
# case (#7837) makes more locals free-eligible, and a free-eligible local's
# overwrite emits a deep drop where an ineligible one emitted the flat
# __fern_rc_dec that reclaims nothing. So the growth IS the reclaim code, paid
# once in .text against a leak that was unbounded in the heap: the examples
# corpus goes from 229,723 stranded allocations to 162,888, a 29% fall.
#
# It trips here and nowhere else because this is one of the three front-end
# slices, where 385 KB is 5.5% — the same bytes are 1.3% of the tracked
# artifact, which stayed inside tolerance. That is the two-tier point above
# working as intended rather than a checker-specific regression.

# WHY THE THREE FRONT-END SLICES SHRANK (-10.8%, -7.9%, -7.6%). Folding a
# uniqueness test on the null pointer. `OpRcIsUnique`'s own declaration says
# "sentinel/static -> 0" and every backend's helper opens with a null guard, so
# `is_unique(null)` is 0 — but `Fold` had no rule for the op, and
# `ConstPropagate` was already delivering a literal `const.i32 0` to 8456 of
# 15582 guards over the conformance corpus. Each one gated a deep drop of a
# slot holding the zero-init constant: an unreachable block of roughly 20 ops.
#
# Every one of the fifteen shrank, from -3.0% (the tracked artifact, 1 MB) to
# -10.8%. Only three breached tolerance, and they are the same front-end slices
# the note above records moving +5.5%: 385 KB is 5.5% of a 7 MB driver and 1.3%
# of a 30 MB one, which is the two-tier point working as intended again.
#
# It does NOT undo that growth. #7837 added deep drops that RUN, against an
# unbounded heap leak; this removes drop blocks that cannot. They are
# independent, and checker_modload_run now sits below its pre-#7837 figure
# (7053860) because the dead blocks predate both.

# 2026-08-31 — every row shrank 12–14.3%, and this is the whole table moving at
# once rather than a per-driver story: PruneZeroSlotGuards (#7787) deletes the
# scope-exit drop a frame emits for a local that was never assigned on the path
# reaching it, which is 10.9% of all IR ops over the self-host compiler. The
# tracked artifact fern.fern goes 30366508 -> 26733284, a 3.63 MB win. Numbers
# are the ones driver-sizes measured, pasted from its own corrected-baseline
# block — none is derived or scaled.

# 2026-09-01 — every row shrank 7.5–10.4%, the whole table again: the x86-64
# assembler now relaxes in-range jmp/jcc to their 2-byte rel8 forms (#7899),
# and every driver here is an x86-64 ELF it links. The tracked artifact goes
# 28080148 -> 25163796. Numbers pasted from driver-sizes' corrected-baseline
# block.

# 2026-09-01 — ten rows GREW 5.4%, two causes, measured apart on irlower_run:
# 18021740 (this table) -> 18279996 on plain main, +1.43% of drift nothing had
# banked, -> 19046076 with #6993's env-box lift on astwalk's accumulator spine,
# +4.19% more. The tracked artifact fern.fern goes 25163796 -> 26649772, +5.9%:
# it links every backend, so it pays the instantiation about twice over. It
# surfaced a run later than the rest only because the job reporting it is a
# different one — nothing about it was inside tolerance. The four small drivers
# (asm_ir_elig, checker_modload, ssa_run, ssa_emit) land at +1.2-1.5% and keep
# their numbers.
#
# The +4.19% is one monomorphised instantiation: map_expr_acc at InlineCloAcc
# is 2.1 MB of asm, map_stmt_acc 1.1 MB. The multiplier is the accumulator
# OWNING HEAP, not the walk being generic — the same fold_expr_nodes costs
# 28 KB at i32 and 353 KB at string, 13x for the type argument alone, and a
# rewriting spine reconstructs every node on top of that. Consumers added later
# at the SAME T are free; a new heap-owning T costs this again. So prefer a
# scalar or index-like accumulator when a pass can be written that way (#6993).
#
# Banked with the growth understood rather than after the fact, which is the
# thing #6826 was written to prevent. Behaviour is unchanged: the whole
# compiler emitted through the pre- and post-port compilers is byte-identical
# on x86-64 and wasm.

# 2026-09-02 — three rows grew past tolerance; the other twelve moved +0.5-4.6%
# and keep their numbers. One commit tips all three: 78045cb (ir: reclaim own
# accumulators through recursion and variant-payload temps). Bisected on
# checker_modload_run over the 86 commits since the previous refresh, then
# confirmed on the other two. Those deltas were measured with the in-process
# linker rather than CI's asm-plus-gcc path, so read them as deltas and not
# against the figures below:
#
#   checker_modload_run   3748748 -> 4019084   (+7.2%, and its whole breach)
#   asm_load_run         15943420 -> 16541436  (+3.8%, on +1.0% of prior drift)
#   fern.fern            19648332 -> 20250444  (+3.1%, on +3.4% of prior drift)
#
# The growth is reclaim code, as #7837's was: seeding findReturnsFreshBox with
# an `own` parameter keeps a threaded accumulator free-eligible, and crediting a
# variant-constructor payload store makes more locals emit a deep drop where a
# flat __fern_rc_dec stood. It buys the leaks that commit's census takes to zero
# — own-accumulator recursion 100-256 blocks, string-keyed ordmap insert 1637,
# pmap insert 500. checker_modload_run breaches on 78045cb alone; the other two
# were already carrying drift nothing had banked and cross the line with it.
#
# Numbers pasted from driver-sizes' corrected-baseline block.

# 2026-09-04 — every row shrank 5.8-8.5%, the whole table at once: the inline
# rc guards stopped testing what the below-heap compare already rejects (#8193).
# Both natives emit that guard at every inc and dec site, so removing two
# instructions from each is a whole-table effect rather than a per-driver one.
# The tracked artifact fern.fern goes 14647852 -> 13607468, a 1.04 MB win.
#
# This baseline is one refresh late. #8202 landed the change without it, which
# left driver-sizes red on main for the interval — the failure mode the SHRINK
# check exists to catch, doing its job. Numbers pasted from that job's own
# corrected-baseline block, on the head that carried the change.

# 2026-09-04 — twelve rows shrink 13.4-21.5%, the whole table together: the
# #4873 caller-side containment bracket stops retaining a struct field the
# caller cannot read back (#7397). The bracket is emitted around every call
# whose struct argument survives it, for every array field of that argument's
# type, so removing the unobservable ones takes emitted code out of every
# driver rather than one backend's rows. The tracked artifact fern.fern goes
# 13898620 -> 11780988.
#
# These figures were pinned onto main a PR early, by #8233, which read them
# off a head that carried this branch and credited them to #8178. They belong
# here, where the change that produces them lives. driver-sizes on this branch
# is green against them; main's, without this branch, measures the larger set
# #8234 restored.
#
# checker_modload_run, ssa_emit_run and ssa_run are inside the 5% band and the
# job did not list them.

# 2026-09-05 — twelve rows grew 5.3-9.4%, the three front-end slices shrank
# 1.8-2.6%, and all fifteen are refreshed. One commit carries the growth:
# 1df1072 (selfhost(#8179): box LowerState's per-function facts as LowerFrame).
# Measured on irlower_run, the dedicated irlower driver, with CI's own method
# (TestSelfHostWarmStockDriver at the commit, gcc link):
#
#   bbab1a8 (its parent)   6956444   +1.9% of drift on the previous table
#   1df1072                7431580   +6.8% in the one commit
#   509aa8f (main)         7431580   nothing after it moved this driver
#
# The last figure is CI's figure for main to the byte, and every byte of the
# step is in the R E segment (0x698ec2 -> 0x70ccd0); the RW segment is
# identical. The three drivers that do not link irlower.fern are the three
# that shrank. The commit's own measurement is instructions executed (-1.82%
# Ir on a checker.fern compile, from spreading 9 rc fields per LowerState
# copy instead of 41); this is the .text the frame indirection costs at its
# 702 read sites and 13 whole-frame rebuilds. Numbers pasted from
# driver-sizes' union on 509aa8f, main's own run, which was red on them.

# 2026-09-06 — checker_modload_run alone, 1963372 -> 2151348 (+9.6%), and the
# other fourteen rows are inside the band and unchanged. Two commits carry the
# step, both in #8720 (selfhost #8445, mirroring E076/E077 into the self-host
# checker). Measured with CI's own method — TestSelfHostWarmStockDriver at each
# commit — on this file's terms:
#
#   2e9424d (#8718)   2084852   the last commit before the step
#   58c8ba9           2143156   +58,304 B — "mirror E076 and E077"
#   dfc22ea           2151348   +8,192 B — "fold top-level consts into defaults"
#   967393a (main)    2151348   nothing after it moved this driver
#
# The last figure is CI's figure for this PR's head to the byte, and this
# branch measures the same 2151348 as main does: none of the growth is its own.
# The walk also discriminates, which an agreeing number alone does not show —
# it moves 2109332 -> 2084852 -> 2143156 -> 2151348 across the sampled range,
# following the source rather than the checkout.
#
# TWO EARLIER MOVES ARE FOLDED INTO THIS ROW, because the baseline outlasted
# them both. 1963372 was already stale by #8682, where the driver measures
# 2109332; #8712 then SHRANK it to 2084852 and nothing recorded that either.
# That is precisely the failure the header describes — an un-updated baseline
# after a win silently raises the ceiling the next regression is measured
# against — and it is why a +9.6% breach names a +2.8% commit. Only the step
# above is attributed to a commit; the two before it are recorded as observed,
# not credited to a change this pass did not isolate.

# Refreshed downward after preserving nested field roots in grow containment.
# Same-source A/B measurements and the cause are recorded in
# docs/SELFHOST-GROW-BRACKET-SIZE-2026-09-08.md. No ceiling was increased.
# Measured after lexical capture contracts and removal of inert null cleanup.
# Attribution: docs/SELFHOST-LEXICAL-CAPTURE-SIZE.md. Partial drivers now link
# checked capture resolution; the whole compiler shrinks against its PR parent.
# 2026-09-13 — all fifteen rows are what CI links at #9193's head. Its parent
# already linked 4.4–4.96% above the rows before it, and the `.with`
# copy-on-write adds 4,176–8,272 B to each driver carrying a self-reassign
# site (same-toolchain A/B in docs/rc-log/2026-09-13-with-cow-runtime-count.md).
# The CLI now links the typed semantic production pipeline. The measured
# linkage cost, prior removal of unnecessary linkage from partial drivers,
# and remaining source growth are recorded in
# docs/SELFHOST-SEMANTIC-PRODUCTION-SIZE.md. Only the CLI row is refreshed.
# 2026-09-16 — asm_run alone, 7684164 -> 8112056 (+5.6%): the x86-64 backend
# gained the SSA emitter of #9494. The three drivers that link both native
# backends were refreshed with #9484 and move 0.2% here; the rest are inside
# the band. Number pasted from driver-sizes' own report.
# 2026-09-16 — the three drivers that link asm_arm64_ir grew 5.2-5.7%
# (asm_load_run, asm_modload_run, asm_ir_run) and are refreshed; the other
# twelve moved +1.3-3.5% and keep their rows. The arm64 backend gained the SSA
# emitter of #9484 and with it links ssa_lift, the allocator and the pruning
# pass; drivers that do not link that backend moved by the same 1.3-3.5% of
# drift in the same run, so about half of each refreshed delta is drift and
# the rest is the backend. Numbers pasted from driver-sizes' own report.
# 2026-09-26 — checker_modload_run alone, 2663732 -> 2802364 (+5.2%). The
# front end already linked +4.9% on #10321's head; #10328's literal-match
# desugar (the cached scrutinee, boolean arms, the value-position block) and
# the checker's function-typed value local add the last ~8 KB. The other
# eleven rows moved +1.9-4.2% of drift in the same run and keep their rows.
# Number pasted from driver-sizes' own report.
# 2026-09-28 — fern.fern alone, 13753865 -> 14118057 (+2.65%, inside the
# band). The CLI links the WIT decoder and composer and the embedded proxy
# world for `-target wasm32-wasi-http` (wit_decode, wit_compose,
# wit_proxy_world: ~1,450 lines that no driver linked before), and the wasm
# extern bridge gained its heap-payload result wrappers. Measured with
# FERN_WARM_DRIVER=fern.fern FERN_DRIVER_SIZE_REPORT on the branch.
# 2026-09-29 — every row re-baselined: the drivers are built by the pinned
# stage0 self-host compiler instead of the Go x86-64 backend (#10680), and
# its output is 12-27% smaller per driver (fern.fern 14118057 -> 12342352).
# fern.fern/stage2 joins as the tracked artifact — the compiler's own output
# for itself, the one row a codegen change in the current compiler moves.
# Measured with FERN_WARM_DRIVER over every row, FERN_DRIVER_SIZE_REPORT on
# the branch. Re-measured the same day against the refreshed pin
# stage0-20260929-32d575e, whose hand-back set copies a lent view for a
# callee that keeps it through a local (every row +0.005-0.04%, fern.fern
# 12342352 -> 12346904, the copies that fix carries), and once more on the
# merge of main at c2160d3ce, which changed the driver sources and the
# stdlib they compile in (+0.004% to +0.025% per row over the previous
# merge, fern.fern 12346904 -> 12346536 across both). Equal to fern.fern in
# size on that tree: six commits to compiler landed after the
# pin's source commit 32d575e60 (740b49209 ssarc.fern, 319a4a50e
# ssasem.fern, d5792c908 read_all_stdin, aee0e4136 parser.fern, 067f7462a
# checker.fern, 02196de0a irlower.fern) and none moved the stage2 byte
# count off stage1's. One that does will part the two (docs/BOOTSTRAP.md).
# 2026-09-29 — asm_ir_run alone, 7302608 -> 9080328 (+24.3%). The driver
# lowers through the typed path (semlower) and links both lowerings until the
# AST one retires (#10659). The other rows are unchanged. Number pasted from
# driver-sizes' own report on run 36612302644.
# 2026-09-30 — asm_run 6765464 -> 8648888 (+27.8%), asm_load_run 8099152 ->
# 9294032 (+14.8%), asm_modload_run 7556384 -> 9438224 (+24.9%). The three
# drivers' merged emit lowers through the typed path (semlower) and links
# both lowerings until the AST one retires. Measured with
# TestSelfHostWarmStockDriver on the pinned stage0.
# 2026-09-30 — wasm_ir_run 6704912 -> 8820144 (+31.5%), wasm_run 6702024 ->
# 8817328 (+31.6%), wasm_runio_run 6671832 -> 8816656 (+32.1%),
# asm_load_run 9294032 -> 10514488 (+13.1%). The wasm drivers emit through
# the typed path (semlower) and link both lowerings until the AST one
# retires; asm_load_run's wasm32-wasi leg emits over the typed path too, and
# gains -emit component-core. Measured with TestSelfHostWarmStockDriver on
# the pinned stage0, on main at 083167101 with this change merged.
# 2026-10-01 — asm_ir_run 9080328 -> 9619240 (+5.9%), asm_ir_elig_run
# 4627344 -> 4881280 (+5.5%), checker_modload_run 2220984 -> 2335496 (+5.2%);
# the other ten rows grew 2.5-4.9% in the same run and keep their numbers.
# Each breach is three movements, measured apart with CI's own method
# (TestSelfHostWarmStockDriver; the last column is CI's figure to the byte):
#
#                         main 7f9076b   +#10881 src   +pin 7d8ea4e
#   asm_ir_run            9466992 +4.3%  9476728 +0.1%  9619240 +1.5%
#   asm_ir_elig_run       4772448 +3.1%  4779360 +0.2%  4881280 +2.1%
#   checker_modload_run   2313848 +4.2%  2322352 +0.4%  2335496 +0.6%
#
# The first column is main's own drift since the last refresh, unbanked, on
# the old pin (stage0-20260929-32d575e). The second is this PR's source: the
# parser's generic union aliases, their printer inverse and the checker's
# enum-arity rule (#10764). The third is the refreshed pin's code generation:
# the same sources compiled by stage0-20261001-7d8ea4e, which carries main's
# self-host commits from 32d575e60 to 7d8ea4e18 (the map str key column and
